channel.title: Updated · Tech
channel.description: Chips, software, security, devices and space (beyond AI)

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach Cloud One, the US Air Force's main cloud platform, halting updates and migrations
item.description: Reuters reports that hackers exploited a software flaw to reach the control layer of Cloud One, the Air Force's cloud platform; the attackers and any data loss are unknown. (BleepingComputer, Engadget)

item.title: An unpatched flaw in the Cacti network monitoring tool is published with working attack code and no warning to developers
item.description: A researcher published a working exploit for an unpatched Cacti flaw that lets outsiders run commands when guest access is on; administrators should disable the guest account. (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News)

item.title: FIFA confirms a cyberattack exposed personal and business information after a new group claimed to leak 12 GB of files
item.description: FIFA says hackers accessed a "limited set of personal and business information"; a group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims it took more than 12 GB of internal files. (SecurityWeek (AP), Infosecurity Magazine)

item.title: Microsoft issues an emergency fix after its November no-restart update crashes some Windows Server 2025 machines
item.description: Microsoft released an out-of-band update, KB5138318, for Windows Server 2025 machines that could crash when an IPv6 route expired after November's hotpatch. (The Register, BleepingComputer)

item.title: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
item.description: Encrypted vector databases that reveal which records are returned together leak the records' topics: an attack called SAGE recovers category labels with up to 84.3% accuracy. (Yang Zhang, Ruiqi He, Xiaoqian Sun et al. · Nankai University)

item.title: A 12-year-old flaw in the Linux kernel's NFS file server lets remote attackers gain root without logging in
item.description: Security firm OpenSec detailed NFS2ROOT, a critical flaw present in Linux's built-in NFS server since 2014 that lets an unauthenticated attacker who can reach port 2049 take full control. (OpenSec, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Britain's Department for Work and Pensions takes online services offline after a cyber incident
item.description: The UK department that pays the state pension and benefits said it took some online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident, and that regular payments are not affected. (The Record, The Register)

item.title: SAP confirms suspicious activity in its systems after Der Spiegel reports attackers altered its source code on GitHub
item.description: SAP says it found suspicious activity and sees no evidence that customer business data was accessed; Der Spiegel reports that attackers stole employees' GitHub tokens and copied and modified source code. (BleepingComputer, t-online, Security Affairs)

item.title: Google will publish the phone numbers and addresses of money-making Android developers worldwide from March 2027
item.description: To comply with EU and UK rules, Google will show a phone number and address for every Play Store developer classed as a trader, visible to users everywhere and with no PO boxes allowed. (The Verge, Engadget)

item.title: 1Password says an attacker used an employee's GitHub account to steal customer names and emails, but not password vaults
item.description: 1Password disclosed that an attacker who took over an employee's GitHub account planted code in its backend and downloaded customer account records, while password vaults and their encryption keys stayed out of reach. (TechCrunch, BleepingComputer)

item.title: The FCC conditionally authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites as orbital data centers
item.description: The FCC gave SpaceX conditional approval for a constellation of up to 1 million data-center satellites, with 14 years to deploy it, while withholding a waiver on how retired satellites are disposed of. (Ars Technica, TechCrunch)

item.title: Palo Alto Networks confirms attackers are exploiting the Fragnesia Linux flaw on firewalls with internet-exposed management interfaces
item.description: Palo Alto Networks says attackers are chaining a PHP flaw with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw against PAN-OS firewalls whose management interface faces the internet, and has released fixes. (BleepingComputer, Palo Alto Networks)

item.title: Drupal confirms attackers are exploiting a highly critical installer flaw to take over unpatched websites
item.description: Drupal says an installer flaw patched on November 18 has been exploited on live sites since November 19; CISA ordered US federal agencies to fix it by Friday. (BleepingComputer, Drupal.org)

item.title: Reducing RSA-2048 Factoring Resources Below One Billion Toffolis via LLM-Driven Verifiable Quantum Compilation
item.description: A redesigned circuit for factoring 2048-bit RSA numbers on a quantum computer needs fewer than one billion Toffoli gates, down from billions, at roughly 1,300 to 2,900 logical qubits. (Xiaodi Li, Yuqing Wang, Xue Chen et al. · Intelligent Quantum Inception Co., Ltd. ; Tsinghua University)

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach an unclassified intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and two other US spy agencies
item.description: Unknown attackers reportedly broke into an open-source intelligence system at the CIA, also affecting ODNI and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; a source says no classified networks or data were involved. (BleepingComputer, The Verge, The Record)

item.title: The US Treasury's financial crimes bureau FinCEN takes systems offline after unauthorized access
item.description: FinCEN, the Treasury bureau that receives banks' suspicious-activity reports, says intruders accessed a limited subset of its systems; it took some systems offline and extended filing deadlines. (The Verge, The Record, BleepingComputer)

item.title: A US jury convicts Huawei on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud and sanctions violations
item.description: A federal jury in New York found Huawei and three subsidiaries guilty of stealing US companies' technology, defrauding banks and violating Iran sanctions, but acquitted it of racketeering; sentencing is set for September 2027. (The Verge, The Register)

item.title: Microsoft declares an internal "Code Red" after its November email outage and sets a one-hour target for resolving major incidents
item.description: Internal memos reviewed by Reuters show Microsoft has made reliability work on Microsoft 365 its top engineering priority after the November 12 outage, which a senior executive called the worst in Exchange Online's history. (Ars Technica, The Verge)

item.title: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits
item.description: An automated pipeline using an off-the-shelf language model turned public Linux kernel fixes into 17 verified Android privilege-escalation exploits, while the same fixes took a median of 181 days to reach Pixel phones. (Kareem Shehada, Zhiyun Qian · University of California, Riverside)

item.title: South Korea's power utility KEPCO confirms a breach that exposed data on 1.52 million people, including bank and card numbers
item.description: Korea Electric Power Corporation says an intruder took personal data on about 1.52 million customers, suppliers and staff from its billing platform and procurement system; the privacy regulator has opened an investigation. (Seoul Economic Daily, Seoul Economic Daily (regulator probe), BleepingComputer)

item.title: Nvidia's board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive less than two weeks after his resignation
item.description: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO and president, saying input from senior US government officials convinced it that his return poses no national security risk. (TechCrunch, The Register)

item.title: Amazon buys Decart's chip-optimization software and hires its founders as it prepares to sell Trainium chips to customers
item.description: Amazon is acquiring the Decart Optimization Stack, software that tunes AI workloads for specific chips, along with Decart's founders and engineers, in a deal Bloomberg values at about $7.5 billion. (TechCrunch, The Register)

item.title: German media report that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed anti-satellite weapon into orbit as early as December
item.description: NDR, WDR and Süddeutsche Zeitung report that Western intelligence agencies believe Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, which would threaten thousands of spacecraft in low Earth orbit; the Kremlin dismisses the claim. (Ars Technica, AeroTime)

item.title: Interrupt-Aware Static Detection of Deadlocks in Rust Operating Systems
item.description: A static analysis that tracks both held locks and interrupt state in Rust kernels, paired with an AI agent that audits its reports, found nine maintainer-confirmed deadlock bugs in four Rust operating systems. (Yuzhi Li, Hongliang Tian, Chengjun Chen et al. · Fudan University; Ant Group)

item.title: The FBI investigates an apparent breach of NCIC, the database police across the US use to check warrants and stolen property
item.description: CNN and the Associated Press report that the FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into the National Crime Information Center; the bureau has not confirmed it and the scope is unknown. (BleepingComputer, TechCrunch)

item.title: Microsoft says attackers exploited an Entra Connect Health flaw to read administrator email addresses and tenant details
item.description: A flaw in Microsoft's Entra Connect Health API, present from July 23 until a fix on November 19, let outsiders read administrator contacts and tenant metadata; passwords and tokens were not exposed. (BleepingComputer, Daily CyberSecurity)

item.title: The FCC overrides California's landline rules, clearing AT&T to drop copper phone service for about 184,000 homes
item.description: The FCC ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort rules against AT&T, which wants to end basic copper phone service for 184,000 residential and 15,000 business customers in June 2027. (Ars Technica, Broadband Breakfast)

item.title: F5 issues emergency hotfixes for critical BIG-IP flaws that can crash traffic handling and may allow remote code execution
item.description: F5 released out-of-band hotfixes for critical, unauthenticated BIG-IP flaws that can crash its traffic engine and may allow remote code execution; no mitigations exist besides patching. (BleepingComputer, Canadian Centre for Cyber Security)

item.title: Amazon says suspected Chinese hackers used the AI agent framework Cairn to find and exploit a zero-day at East Asian universities
item.description: Amazon found an exposed Cairn server showing AI agents that worked for hours without human direction, then discovered and used an unknown flaw in a medical imaging app to take over university servers. (The Record, The Register)

item.title: UK surveillance tribunal confirms the Home Office served Apple a secret order over encrypted iCloud data
item.description: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's secrecy argument and confirmed it served Apple a Technical Capability Notice, though the order's content stays secret ahead of a 2027 hearing. (Investigatory Powers Tribunal judgment, The Register)

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots by default to keep Siri and Gemini agents from reading private chats
item.description: Signal's iOS and Android apps now block screenshots by default so built-in AI agents cannot capture chats, and the company says operating systems give developers no robust way to stop such access. (The Register, Engadget)

item.title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Polymorph has an AI agent write one tunable Linux kernel policy, then tunes it live without a language model, beating Linux's defaults for page caching and scheduling at far lower cost than offline search. (Dean Sysman, Georgios Liargkovas, Tal Zussman et al.)

item.title: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm breaches at outside vendors after an extortion gang leaks customer data
item.description: JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard say vendors were breached, exposing customer names and email addresses but no card numbers, after the N0n extortion group posted their data online. (The Register, SecurityWeek)

item.title: Broadcom patches a vCenter flaw that suspected Chinese state hackers exploited since September
item.description: Broadcom issued an emergency fix for a 9.8-rated vCenter Server authentication bypass that Mandiant says a suspected Chinese espionage group used as a zero-day to take over virtualized environments. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: The European Commission confirms a cyberattack in which hackers used a public AI hacking tool
item.description: The European Commission says attackers using a publicly available AI tool disrupted staff payroll, leave and medical reimbursement systems for more than ten days, with no evidence so far of a broad data breach. (The Register, The Record)

item.title: Congress publishes Nvidia and AMD's China chip licences, showing 879,000 AI chips approved
item.description: House committee chair Brian Mast released licence records showing US regulators approved more than 879,000 of 3.4 million requested Nvidia and AMD AI chips for China, including sales to Alibaba and Tencent. (House Foreign Affairs Committee, The Register)

item.title: YUL: Bringing Software Supply Chain Security to Coding Agents
item.description: YUL checks every software dependency a coding agent declares against the package registry and blocks stale or nonexistent versions, so agents end on the latest release in over 90% of affected runs. (Aman Sharma, Frank Reyes, Martin Monperrus · KTH Royal Institute of Technology)

item.title: Attackers publish two credential-stealing versions of Microsoft's official Agent Framework package on PyPI
item.description: Two malicious releases of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package, downloaded about 200,000 times a month, stole cloud and developer credentials; developers who installed versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 should rebuild and rotate secrets. (BleepingComputer, The Register)

item.title: Intel signs its first outside customer for its 18A chip-making process, and Microsoft adopts its EMIB packaging
item.description: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says an unnamed company has signed on to make chips with Intel's 18A-P process, and that 18A yields have reached 70%, a step for Intel's effort to compete with TSMC. (Crypto Briefing, TrendForce)

item.title: Microsoft previews Windows Server 2028, which ships hardened by default with post-quantum key exchange
item.description: Windows Server 2028's public preview turns on hundreds of security settings from first boot, including Kerberos over NTLM and hybrid post-quantum TLS, and Microsoft warns that some older software may break. (BleepingComputer, Ars Technica)
